Layout map layer symbol objects

Source: R/zz-gen-layout.R
go_map_layer_symbol.Rd

The object for the layout's map.layer.symbol (go_map_layer()). go_map_layer_symbol() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_map_layer_symbol(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  icon = NULL,
  iconsize = NULL,
  placement = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  textfont = NULL,
  textposition = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

icon

Sets the symbol icon image (map.layer.layout.icon-image). Full list: https://www.mapbox.com/maki-icons/ String.

iconsize

Sets the symbol icon size (map.layer.layout.icon-size). Has an effect only when `type` is set to "symbol". Number.

placement

Sets the symbol and/or text placement (map.layer.layout.symbol-placement). If `placement` is "point", the label is placed where the geometry is located If `placement` is "line", the label is placed along the line of the geometry If `placement` is "line-center", the label is placed on the center of the geometry One of "point", "line", "line-center".

text

Sets the symbol text (map.layer.layout.text-field). String.

textfont

Sets the icon text font (color=map.layer.paint.text-color, size=map.layer.layout.text-size). Has an effect only when `type` is set to "symbol". A go_font() object or named list, with properties color, family, size, style and weight (see go_font()).

textposition

Sets the positions of the `text` elements with respects to the (x,y) coordinates. One of "top left", "top center", "top right", "middle left", "middle center", "middle right", "bottom left", "bottom center", "bottom right".

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_layout_map_layer_symbol object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

quakes |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(lat = ~lat, lon = ~long) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      layers = list(
        go_map_layer(symbol = go_map_layer_symbol(text = "title"))
      )
    )
  )
